newsitem.title: UK: Hyder says cost cutting ahead of target.
newsitem.headline: Hyder says cost cutting ahead of target.

text.p: British multi-utility Hyder Plc said on Monday that cost reduction programmes in its electricity, water and services businesses continued ahead of target.

The company, which said pre-tax profits for the year were 208.2 million pounds ($339.8 million) and paid out a total dividend of 43.9 pence per share, said savings from the merger of Welsh Water and South Wales Electricity (Swalec), the regional electricity company which it took over, were 11.5 million pounds.
"Operating two utilities in the same geography continues to generate significant efficiences and gave rise to earnings enhancement in excess of 17 percent in the year," Hyder said in a statement.

Hyder said its gearing rose to 100 percent from 95 percent in the previous period while its programme to cut costs at the electricity business by 45 million pounds a year was 90 percent secured by March 31, 1997 with potential for finding "greater synergies than originally identified".

But it added that "in the longer term, utility efficiency benefits will become increasingly difficult to achieve and have focused on ways of growing our non-regulated profits to underpin long-term dividend growth."

The company said profit before interest from its non-regulated activities was 32.6 million pounds or 11.5 percent of the total and said it had "a strong foundation on which to build on our wider infrastructure aspirations".
